headline: Ransomware gang claims Michigan State incident; Germany flags spyware on lawmakers' iPhones; GitLab RCE attacks continue

bullets.text: New: The Record reports the ransomware gang behind a recent hospital attack has claimed a cyber incident at Michigan State.
New: TechCrunch reports Germany says lawmakers' iPhones may have been hacked with spyware.

BleepingComputer reports over 1,000 GitLab servers are vulnerable to ongoing RCE attacks. CISA KEV lists GitLab CE/EE flaw CVE-2026-97229, whose federal due date passed on 2026-11-01. Alpine Linux rebuilt its GitLab after an attempted RCE attack.

Connect Secure, 4 outlets: Ivanti patched two more zero-days chained in attacks, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-104935 in the same product, with federal due dates of today, 2026-11-02, and 2026-11-13.

Claude, 4 outlets: SecurityWeek reports a malicious Claude Code extension served in a Cursor supply chain attack. BleepingComputer says it planted SSH backdoors. Separately, The Hacker News reports the VOLTA infostealer uses Claude, Gemini and Kimi AI to rank victims by financial value.

Binance, 6 outlets: The Register reports the FBI pins the $6.3B heist on North Korean hackers. The Record names TraderTraitor and says the FBI urges the crypto industry to block transactions; SecurityWeek says it flagged over 600 addresses.

actions: Patch GitLab CE/EE (CVE-2026-97229) and Cisco ASA/FTD (CVE-2026-76418) now; both KEV due dates have passed. Check GitLab servers for signs of RCE.
Apply Ivanti's latest Connect Secure patches today, covering CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, and check appliances for compromise.
Find any Langflow, LXD and MicroCloud servers, check vendor advisories for the critical flaws, and patch. Restrict access to any you cannot patch yet.
If developers use the Claude Code extension in Cursor, check it against the vendor advisory and look for unexpected SSH keys or services.
Review infostealer detections, and rotate credentials and tokens on any host found infected.
If you handle crypto transactions, screen against the addresses the FBI flagged for the Binance heist, and warn staff about Binance-themed scams.
